title: A gate naming SECRET_TOKENS, PASSWORD_TOKENS or PRIVATE_TOKENS is classed design since token-count identifiers are blanked whole
goal: The token-count identifier rule BG-xp3imb24 added (bl_authority.TOKEN_IDENT) blanks a whole upper-case identifier ending in TOKENS unless one of its parts is a CRED_WORDS word, so the secret word inside it (SECRET_TOKENS, PASSWORD_TOKENS, PRIVATE_TOKENS, KEY_TOKENS) is removed too and the gate falls from secrets to design, a fail-open regression found by the SP-uzwbt63u review; an identifier any of whose parts is a secret word (secret, password, passphrase, private, key, credential, pat, ssh, or a CRED_WORDS word) keeps the secrets class, while DISPATCH_BASE_TOKENS, MAX_TOKENS and JUDGE_REPLY_TOKENS stay design

run: import sys; sys.path.insert(0, '_tools'); import bl_authority as a; c = lambda q: a.class_reasons({'touches': []}, {'id': 'g', 'question': q, 'options': []})[0]; s = [c('Is ' + n + ' used?') for n in ('SECRET_TOKENS', 'PASSWORD_TOKENS', 'PRIVATE_TOKENS', 'KEY_TOKENS', 'API_TOKENS')]; d = [c('What is census.' + n + '?') for n in ('DISPATCH_BASE_TOKENS', 'MAX_TOKENS', 'JUDGE_REPLY_TOKENS')]; sys.exit(0 if s == ['secrets'] * 5 and d == ['design'] * 3 else 1)

gates.question: Should the part words of a token-count identifier that keep the class also match with a plural s ending (the goal lists the singular words only)?
options: accept a plural s on the part words
gates.recommendation: accept a plural s on the part words
gates.answer: accept a plural s on the part words

notes: Found by the SP-uzwbt63u review (fresh-context reviewer, 2026-10-13), filed S1 by the orchestrator acting as operator: it weakens the operator-only secrets class (fail open), which the policy keeps conservative. Repro run on main 2026-10-13: SECRET_TOKENS, PASSWORD_TOKENS, PRIVATE_TOKENS, KEY_TOKENS class design, API_TOKENS secrets; the three count constants design (exit 1). Before 330b88ba0 all five were secrets.
